artifacts.summary: Parity analysis of the standalone Playwright verify script vs. the MCP server; recommends keeping the batch script (determinism, cost, blank-check fidelity) while adding MCP tools as an optional ad hoc single-slide debugging capability, plus the required present-extension permission-grant plumbing (new settings-fragment.json + manifest merge_targets.settings entry) since present/founder do not inherit web's grants.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's extension system, a domain-specific MCP permission grant (settings-fragment.json permissions.allow) does NOT propagate across extensions unless the consuming extension either (a) declares the granting extension as a manifest dependency (auto-load, but pulls in all of its agents/skills/rules too) or (b) has its own settings-fragment.json copying the grant. Extensions with overlapping tool needs (e.g. web, present, founder all wanting Playwright MCP tools) each need their own settings-fragment.json enumeration under the safe/unsafe carve-out rule -- a wildcard cannot express a safe/unsafe split, so this duplication is accepted, documented drift, not a bug to fix by wildcarding.

When a codebase pins an npm package (e.g. playwright-chromium) for two independent reasons -- a third-party tool's own internal dependency (Slidev's `slidev export` PDF pipeline) and a project's own custom script (a verify script's browser automation loop) -- removing the custom script does NOT remove the npm install requirement. Before recommending 'remove the duplicate install,' separate which consumer actually owns the dependency; only the consumer being deprecated is in scope for removal.

MCP tool-based browser verification (Playwright MCP) fundamentally cannot replicate a standalone script's deterministic exit-code/CI/no-agent-in-the-loop invocation, and is materially more expensive per-check (one agent tool-call round trip per navigate/inspect step vs. one script invocation covering N slides). When comparing a standalone automation script against an MCP-tool equivalent, weigh these two axes explicitly rather than assuming the MCP path is a strict upgrade -- a 'keep the script for batch/CI use, add MCP for ad hoc single-item debugging' split is often the correct outcome rather than full migration.
